events.reason: epigastric pain radiating to the back, vomiting

reports.text: Gallbladder without stones or wall thickening. Common bile duct not dilated; no intrahepatic biliary dilation. Pancreas partly obscured by bowel gas. Liver normal in size. Kidneys normal in size without hydronephrosis. Spleen normal.
reports.conclusion: No gallstones or biliary ductal dilatation.

documents.title: Hospital discharge summary
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
Regional hospital. Admitted 7/2/2024, discharged 7/19/2024.

Principal diagnosis: severe acute pancreatitis, alcohol-induced, with organ failure.
Secondary: acute kidney injury; ANCA vasculitis in remission; acromegaly; hypertension; asthma; alcohol use disorder.

Presentation: one day of intense upper abdominal pain boring through to the back, with nausea and repeated vomiting, after a week of very heavy drinking. Febrile 38.3, HR 110, RR 22, BP 90/60. Abdomen distended and tender throughout with quiet bowel sounds.
Labs: WBC 16.0, Hct 48, BUN 36, amylase 1200, lipase 2500, calcium 7.8, CRP 150.
Ultrasound: no gallstones, no biliary dilation.

Course: Over the first two days he became more unwell despite aggressive IV fluids, with ongoing hypotension, low urine output and a climbing oxygen requirement. Transferred to the ICU: norepinephrine for blood pressure support, heated high-flow oxygen, continued fluids. No dialysis needed; urine output and creatinine recovered over the following week. Weaned off pressors and oxygen, diet advanced.

Alcohol: counseled on complete abstinence; he states he plans to stop.
Discharge medications: lisinopril 20 mg daily, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily, albuterol as needed, octreotide LAR per endocrinology.
Allergies: NKDA
Follow-up: PCP 1 to 2 weeks.

documents.title: Keith in hospital
documents.author: patient
documents.body: This is Keith's wife writing on his account. He was admitted Tuesday with pancreatitis and they moved him to the ICU Thursday. His pressure dropped and they have him on oxygen. I don't know what you can do but I wanted you to know.

documents.title: RE: Keith in hospital
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thank you for letting me know, and I'm sorry you're going through this. The ICU team is the right place for him right now. Please call or message when he's home so we can see him that week. If you want to talk anything through, the office line reaches me.

documents.title: Records request
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: PCP asked for hospital records from July admission. No discharge summary received and pt has not booked a follow-up. Faxed request to hospital HIM. Left VM for pt to schedule hospital follow-up.

documents.title: Refill request
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Lisinopril 20 and HCTZ 25 refill request, 90 days. Last seen 6/5. Hospital summary from July now in chart. Routed to PCP.

documents.title: Refill approved
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: OK for 90 days. Needs a visit with labs before the next fill; please reach out to schedule.

documents.title: Time for your visit and flu shot
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Hi Keith, Dr. asked us to reach out. You are due for a follow-up after your hospital stay and your physical, and flu and COVID vaccines are available now. Reply here or call and we'll find a time that works around your job sites.

events.reason: sudden severe headache, blurred vision, confusion

reports.text:
Indication: thunderclap headache, ophthalmoplegia, known pituitary macroadenoma.
The sellar mass is larger than on the prior study, with signal consistent with recent hemorrhage within it. Ventricles normal in size. No other intracranial hemorrhage. No acute infarct.
reports.conclusion: Enlarged sellar mass with recent hemorrhage, consistent with pituitary apoplexy.

documents.title: Hospital discharge summary
documents.author: intensive care
documents.body:
Regional hospital. Admitted 1/9/2025 through the ED to the ICU; discharged 1/17/2025.

Diagnoses: pituitary apoplexy (hemorrhage into known macroadenoma) with secondary adrenal insufficiency presenting as adrenal crisis.
Background: acromegaly on octreotide LAR, ANCA vasculitis (GPA/MPA) on rituximab maintenance, severe alcohol pancreatitis 7/2024, hypertension, asthma, alcohol use disorder. Before this admission he had been worked up elsewhere for fatigue, reduced libido and some weight gain without any treatment started.

Presentation: abrupt onset of the worst headache he has had, with nausea and blurry vision. His wife found him muddled and struggling to name everyday things. No anticoagulant use.
T 36.8, BP 88/54, HR 118, RR 22. Sweaty and agitated. Both eyelids drooping, eye movements limited, peripheral vision reduced to confrontation. Heart and lungs normal.
Labs: mild hyponatremia, hypoglycemia.
MRI: enlarged sellar mass with recent hemorrhage.

Course: stress-dose IV hydrocortisone and fluids with prompt rise in blood pressure, correction of sodium and glucose, and clearing of confusion. Neurosurgery and endocrinology followed; with steady improvement in eye movements and vision, managed without surgery. Ptosis and eye movement improving at discharge. Octreotide continued.

Discharge medications: hydrocortisone 15 mg each morning and 5 mg mid-afternoon (double for fever or illness, emergency injection kit, medical alert ID advised); lisinopril 20 mg daily; hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily; albuterol as needed; octreotide LAR monthly.
Allergies: NKDA
Follow-up: endocrinology 2 weeks, neuro-ophthalmology, PCP.

documents.title: Hospital records reviewed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Discharge summary for the January ICU stay received and reviewed: pituitary apoplexy with adrenal crisis, managed without surgery, discharged on hydrocortisone via endocrinology. Pt has not been in since last June. Filed; will reconcile when he comes in.

documents.title: Refill request, hydrocortisone
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy sent refill request for hydrocortisone 10 mg and 5 mg tablets, original prescriber a hospital physician. Not on our med list. Routed to PCP.

documents.title: Call with patient
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Per PCP called pt about hydrocortisone. He says he was in the ICU last month, bleed into the pituitary tumor, now on hydrocortisone for life. Taking 15 mg morning and 5 mg mid-afternoon. Has an endocrinology visit Thursday. Advised him to have endocrinology take over the prescription and confirmed he has enough until then (about 10 days). Reviewed doubling dose if sick and going to the ED if vomiting and can't keep it down. Records request sent to hospital. Pt said he would schedule with us but did not want to set a date today.

documents.title: Refill request
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Lisinopril and HCTZ refilled x 90 days. Hospital summary from January reviewed (apoplexy, adrenal insufficiency, hydrocortisone via endocrinology). Has not been seen since last June despite outreach. Front desk to try again.

documents.title: News
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Figured I should tell you. They found a lymphoma last week, the oncologist called it high grade B cell. Chemo is supposed to start Saturday. I know I owe you a visit.

documents.title: RE: News
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Keith, thank you for telling me. I'm sorry. You don't owe me anything, but I'd like to stay in the loop. Please ask the oncology office to copy me on their notes. Keep taking your hydrocortisone, and remember to double it if you get sick during chemo. Message me any time.

reports.text: Sinus rhythm, rate 96. Normal axis. Peaked T waves in the precordial leads. No ST elevation.
reports.conclusion: Peaked T waves, consistent with hyperkalemia.

documents.title: Emergency department record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital ED, 7/3/2025

53 year old man with acromegaly from a pituitary macroadenoma, apoplexy in January now on hydrocortisone, ANCA vasculitis (GPA/MPA), prior alcohol pancreatitis, and alcohol use disorder. High-grade B-cell lymphoma diagnosed a week ago; first chemotherapy planned in two days. Here with nausea, vomiting and lethargy. Denies fever, cough or diarrhea.

BP 145/90, HR 98. Awake and oriented but fatigued. No palpable lymph nodes, no liver or spleen enlargement.
Na 138, K 6.5, Cl 100, HCO3 22, BUN 28, creatinine 2.1 (baseline 1.0), uric acid 12, calcium 7.8, phosphorus 6.5.
ECG: peaked T waves.

Impression: spontaneous tumor lysis syndrome with hyperkalemia and acute kidney injury before chemotherapy.
Treatment: IV calcium gluconate, IV insulin with dextrose, rasburicase, IV fluids; stress-dose hydrocortisone given. Oncology consulted; admitted to the oncology service. Chemotherapy to be postponed until kidney function and electrolytes recover.
Allergies: NKDA

documents.title: ED record reviewed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: ED record 7/3 reviewed: spontaneous tumor lysis before first chemo, K 6.5, creatinine 2.1, admitted to oncology. No inpatient summary yet. Chemo postponed per ED note.

reports.text: Sinus rhythm, rate 98. Peaked T waves. Intervals normal.

documents.title: Hospital discharge summary
documents.author: hematology/oncology
documents.body:
Regional hospital. Admitted 8/9/2025 (ICU), discharged 8/14/2025.

Diagnosis: tumor lysis syndrome after cycle 1 of R-CHOP for diffuse large B-cell lymphoma; acute kidney injury; hyperkalemia.
History: DLBCL diagnosed 6/2025; spontaneous tumor lysis 7/2025 delayed treatment. Cycle 1 R-CHOP given 8/7 with allopurinol and IV hydration. Also acromegaly, secondary adrenal insufficiency after pituitary apoplexy on hydrocortisone, ANCA vasculitis, prior pancreatitis, hypertension, asthma, alcohol use disorder.

Presentation, 48 hours after cycle 1: nausea, vomiting, lethargy and muscle cramping. Tired-appearing. T 37.2, BP 130/85, HR 98, RR 18. Mildly tender in both flanks.
Na 138, K 6.2, Cl 100, HCO3 22, BUN 28, creatinine 2.1 (baseline 0.9), calcium 7.2, phosphorus 6.5, uric acid 12. ECG with peaked T waves.

Course: ICU for cardiac monitoring. IV calcium gluconate, insulin with dextrose, rasburicase, aggressive IV fluids; stress-dose hydrocortisone. Potassium and phosphorus normalized over 72 hours, creatinine improving. No dialysis.
Discharge medications: allopurinol 300 mg daily through cycle 2; hydrocortisone 15 mg AM / 5 mg afternoon; lisinopril 20 mg daily; hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily; albuterol as needed.
Allergies: NKDA
Follow-up: oncology clinic in 1 week; cycle 2 planned on schedule with TLS precautions.

documents.title: Records request
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: PCP requested records of August hospital stay (pt mentioned ICU in a message to the pharmacy line). Faxed request to hospital HIM and to the oncology office for treatment notes.

documents.title: Refill request
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Albuterol HFA refill request. Sent per protocol, he is mid-chemo per his messages. Lisinopril/HCTZ not requested this time.

documents.title: Done with chemo
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Finished my 6th round of R-CHOP on November 20. Had the PET scan last Thursday and the oncologist says there's no active cancer left, complete response. Thought you'd want to know some good news for a change.

documents.title: RE: Done with chemo
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: That is wonderful news, Keith, thank you for sharing it. Please ask oncology to send me the PET report and their summary. When you're up for it after the holidays, come in so we can catch up on everything from this past year.

documents.title: Refill request
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Lisinopril 20 and HCTZ 25 refill request. Pharmacy shows regular fills of both. 30 days only. He needs a visit and BMP before more. Front desk to call.

events.reason: right shoulder injury after fall from ladder

reports.text: Right shoulder, AP and axillary views. The humeral head is displaced anteriorly and inferiorly relative to the glenoid. No fracture of the humeral head, greater tuberosity or glenoid rim identified.
Right shoulder, post-reduction AP and axillary views. Humeral head now congruent with the glenoid. No fracture.

documents.title: Emergency department record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital ED, 3/14/2026

53 M with acromegaly, ANCA vasculitis, adrenal insufficiency on hydrocortisone, and DLBCL recently completing chemotherapy. Came off a ladder and landed directly on the right shoulder, with pain right away. 

Exam on arrival: right shoulder contour squared off, acromion prominent, tender anteriorly. Distal sensation and pulses intact.
X-ray: anterior dislocation, no fracture.

Procedural sedation and closed reduction by orthopedics, uncomplicated. Post-reduction film reduced, no fracture.
After reduction he still could not lift the arm out to the side past about 30 degrees and was weak resisting external rotation; sensation normal throughout the arm.
Impression: anterior shoulder dislocation, reduced; suspected rotator cuff tear.
Plan: sling, ice, analgesia; he was told to take his extra hydrocortisone dose today. Orthopedics clinic within 2 weeks for MRI.
Allergies: NKDA. Medications per patient: lisinopril, hydrochlorothiazide, albuterol, hydrocortisone.

documents.title: Your shoulder
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Keith, I just saw the ED record from the 14th. Sorry about the fall. Make sure you get the orthopedic follow-up and MRI they mentioned, and keep taking the extra hydrocortisone if the pain spikes or you feel unwell. Let me know how you're doing.

documents.title: Orthopedics follow-up
documents.author: orthopedics
documents.body:
Outside orthopedic group
Seen 4/2/2026

Right shoulder 3 weeks after anterior dislocation, reduced in the ED. Still weak lifting the arm overhead. Active abduction limited, passive range better. External rotation strength reduced.
MRI right shoulder: full-thickness tear of the supraspinatus tendon. Glenohumeral joint located.
Assessment: right full-thickness supraspinatus tear after anterior dislocation.
Plan: physical therapy twice weekly for 6 to 8 weeks; if strength and function do not come back, arthroscopic repair would be discussed. He prefers to try therapy first. Return 8 weeks.
NKDA.

documents.title: Orthopedics note reviewed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Ortho letter: full-thickness supraspinatus tear on MRI, PT first. Filed.

documents.title: Shoulder and refills
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Shoulder is coming along with PT, still can't get it all the way up. Can you send my blood pressure pills again? I'll call about coming in once things slow down at work.

documents.title: RE: Shoulder and refills
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Glad PT is helping. I sent 30 days of both. I really do need to see you and check your kidney numbers before another refill. It's been almost two years and a lot has happened. Please book anything in the next month.

documents.title: Overdue visit
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Hi Keith, following up on the doctor's message from May. We have early morning openings in August. Please reply or call the office to schedule.
